newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended the week strongly, buoyed by bund futures, but retreated from highs set in the afternoon after U.S. January CPI data showed inflation there under control with a drop of 0.3 percent.
Dealers were disappointed that the market failed to rally further, seeing sellers coming out of the woodwork as some forecast a downturn after recent performance.
"The figures were very good. But everyone is long at the moment and there are people who really want to sell," one said.
Trade in the cash market was no better than moderate, traders said, with bund futures grabbing most of the attention.
The very long end of the curve booked the biggest gains, adding more than a full point. Activity was concentrated in the 2023 loan and the 10-year benchmark, they said.
But some players are looking for a fallback after the solid gains of the last few months. "I think in terms of cyclical moves, we are going to see correction soon in this market," a broker said.

Some analysts, too, see the market fully valued at current levels. All the good fundamental news that has been pushing German and Dutch bond yields down was now priced in, one said, and they were unlikely to drop much further.
Guilders outperformed later in the day, with the 10-year yield discount to bunds widening out to -13 basis points from -10 overnight.
